[codex] ## Custom System Prompt
[codex] 
[codex] Using `claude-with-custom-system-prompt` is optional. The standard `claude` command and the inspection-only `claude-with-proxy` flow are fine for normal development.
[codex] 
[codex] This custom launcher exists because Claude Code's `--system-prompt` flags append to Anthropic's default system prompt instead of replacing it. The mitmproxy addon in `ai-agent-sandbox/system-prompt-addon.py` swaps only the main prompt body in flight and preserves the required prefix blocks. The custom prompt text lives in `ai-agent-sandbox/system-prompt.md`.
[codex] 
[codex] Read those files before changing prompt replacement behavior. Use `claude-with-proxy` when you only need traffic inspection. Use `claude-with-custom-system-prompt` when you specifically want the lean prompt behavior as part of the test or workflow.

[codex] # Budget Analyzer Workspace
[codex] 
[codex] Development environment entry point that runs AI coding agents in a sandboxed Docker container.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Quick Start
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Install [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) and the [Dev Containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers) extension
[codex] 2. Clone and open:
[codex]    ```bash
[codex]    git clone git@github.com:budgetanalyzer/workspace.git
[codex]    cd workspace
[codex]    code .
[codex]    ```
[codex] 3. Click "Reopen in Container" when prompted (first build uses [`ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile`](/ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile))
[codex] 4. Follow [Getting Started](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/development/getting-started.md) to run the system
[codex] 
[codex] ## Security Model
[codex] 
[codex] | Constraint | Mechanism | Config |
[codex] |------------|-----------|--------|
[codex] | Filesystem isolation | Docker container with explicit volume mounts | [docker-compose.yml:13-17](/ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml#L13-L17) |
[codex] | No SSH agent forwarding | `SSH_AUTH_SOCK: ""` in remoteEnv | [devcontainer.json:18](/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json#L18) |
[codex] | Read-only sandbox | `ai-agent-sandbox/` mounted `:ro` — agent cannot modify its own config | [docker-compose.yml:17](/ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml#L17) |
[codex] | No git push | Without SSH credentials, push fails with "Permission denied (publickey)" | (runtime) |
[codex] 
[codex] **Worst case:** `git reset --hard origin/main` and everything disappears. All changes are local and trivially reversible.
[codex] 
[codex] ## What's Inside
[codex] 
[codex] - **Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and AI Session Handler** — globally available with convenience launchers ([details](docs/launch-options.md))
[codex] - **mitmproxy** — HTTPS traffic inspection with CA cert trusted system-wide ([details](docs/traffic-inspection.md))
[codex] - **Playwright + Chromium** — browser automation pre-installed; verify with `playwright install --list`
[codex] - **Node.js 24** — the latest LTS major line from the signed NodeSource repository, compatible with Site Modeler's `>=22` engine requirement
[codex] - **VGG Image Annotator 3.0.13** — pinned standalone human annotation UI with a localhost-only foreground launcher
[codex] - **ImageMagick** — deterministic image metadata, crop, and review-overlay tools (`identify` and `convert`)
[codex] - **Lazy local TLS trust** — verified system, Python, and Chromium trust for the host-managed Budget Analyzer ingress ([details](docs/local-budget-analyzer-tls.md))
[codex] - **actionlint** — GitHub Actions workflow linting available on `PATH`
[codex] 
[codex] ## What's Here
[codex] 
[codex] - `.devcontainer/` — VS Code devcontainer configuration
[codex] - `ai-agent-sandbox/` — Docker sandbox: Dockerfile, compose, entrypoint, scripts, skills, settings overlay (**read-only at runtime**)
[codex] - `scripts/` — workspace utilities (`sync-all.sh`)
[codex] - `AGENTS.md` — AI agent context (injected via SessionStart hook)
[codex] - `docs/` — [launch options](docs/launch-options.md), [traffic inspection](docs/traffic-inspection.md), [design decisions](docs/design-decisions.md)
[codex] 
[codex] ## Run An AI Session Handler Plan
[codex] 
[codex] A fresh container installs `/workspace/ai-session-handler` globally through an editable pipx
[codex] environment. From any repository root, run a plan in that repository's `docs/plans/` directory by
[codex] its filename stem:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] cd /workspace/REPOSITORY
[codex] ai-run PLAN_NAME
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] For example, `ai-run improve-imports --max-phases 1` runs
[codex] `./docs/plans/improve-imports.md` with `ai-session-handler-codex-high`, streams the worker's
[codex] progress, and forwards the phase limit unchanged. Pass `--quiet` explicitly to suppress live worker
[codex] output while retaining the transcript. Set `CODEX_MODEL` when an explicit Codex model is needed.
[codex] Ordinary Python source changes under `/workspace/ai-session-handler/src/` are visible to the global
[codex] commands without a reinstall or image rebuild.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Local Budget Analyzer HTTPS
[codex] 
[codex] After rebuilding the workspace image with the lazy trust tooling, install or
[codex] refresh the host-published public CA before live work against exactly
[codex] `https://app.budgetanalyzer.localhost`:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] ensure-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust
[codex] check-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] If publication is missing, run orchestration `./setup.sh` on the host. Do not
[codex] generate certificates or bypass TLS verification in the container. See
[codex] [Local Budget Analyzer TLS Trust](docs/local-budget-analyzer-tls.md) for the
[codex] ownership flow and diagnostics.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Human-Reviewed Image Tracing
[codex] 
[codex] A rebuilt sandbox image provides [VGG Image Annotator (VIA) 3.0.13](https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/software/via/), an open-source BSD-2-Clause standalone application with ordered polygon, line, and polyline annotations. The build downloads VGG's [official versioned archive](https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/software/via/downloads/via3/via-3.0.13.zip), verifies archive SHA-256 `d16fac5ac83507587845c04644bdbe81896865f2cb963d570bf0f52d48e7d793`, verifies the standalone image annotator SHA-256 `44de1edcee45a0c442dcd028316cdce1647b4fb1a3ca3669b07cd77f39e5fc98`, and preserves the upstream license under `/opt/via-annotator`.
[codex] 
[codex] VIA is a human-operated annotation tool. The human selects and orders every polygon vertex and every two-point line or polyline. ImageMagick may produce deterministic metadata, crops, and review overlays, but automatic edge detection or other automated tracing must never produce authoritative geometry.
[codex] 
[codex] After changing the sandbox image, use **Dev Containers: Rebuild and Reopen in Container** from the VS Code Command Palette. Do not use a normal window reload: the Node.js, VIA, ImageMagick, and browser prerequisites are image contents and are available only after the rebuild completes.
[codex] 
[codex] Verify the rebuilt environment:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] node --version
[codex] via-annotator --version
[codex] via-annotator --check
[codex] identify -version
[codex] convert -version
[codex] playwright --version
[codex] playwright install --list
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] `node --version` must report major version 24, `via-annotator --check` must report a valid 3.0.13 installation without starting a server, and Playwright's list must include Chromium under `/opt/playwright-browsers`.
[codex] 
[codex] Start VIA in a terminal:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] via-annotator
[codex] # Or choose another local port:
[codex] via-annotator --port 8766
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] The default local URL is `http://localhost:8765/via_image_annotator.html`. The launcher remains in the foreground; press `Ctrl+C` in that terminal to stop it cleanly. VIA never starts as a service or background process.
[codex] 
[codex] For private source images, choose **Add Local Files** in VIA and select the original image with the browser file picker. Create the ordered polygon and the required two-point line or polyline annotations manually, then save the VIA project and export its JSON for the reviewed import workflow. The launcher binds strictly to `127.0.0.1` and serves only immutable files in `/opt/via-annotator`; it neither serves `/workspace` nor provides a file-upload endpoint. Selected local files are read in the browser and are not sent to the static server. Do not use remote-file or project-sharing features for private images.
[codex]

[codex] - Individual services: see respective repos

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] 
[codex] This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] [September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] [dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership and policy
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared policy is
[codex] [`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] 
[codex] Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] or upstream support status.
[codex] 
[codex] The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] 
[codex] - historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] - local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex]   inventories
[codex] - first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex]   overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] - Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] - arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Cost and service boundary
[codex] 
[codex] Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] `govulncheck`.
[codex] 
[codex] GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Activation procedure
[codex] 
[codex] Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] prepared and locally validated their files. Phases 1–11 require no credentials;
[codex] all authenticated validation and credential review belong to Phase 12. Agents
[codex] must never receive GitHub, package, registry, or Mend credentials, including in
[codex] Phase 12. The user performs authenticated operations in GitHub/Mend or their own
[codex] trusted environment and supplies sanitized evidence for agent review.
[codex] 
[codex] Missing authentication, authenticated-only API access, and unauthenticated API
[codex] rate limits are recorded as pending Phase 12 evidence; they do not block local
[codex] configuration preparation. This includes private Maven resolution, complete
[codex] remotely resolved Java snapshots, graph submission, published-preset resolution,
[codex] and hosted bot/scanner runs. Local schema validation, extraction, workflow lint,
[codex] and checks that can run without credentials remain required. Preserve actual
[codex] failures and incomplete outputs; never report a deferred check as passed or
[codex] weaken a hosted job's failure behavior. Non-authentication prerequisites and
[codex] implementation defects remain blockers under the owning repository's rules.
[codex] 
[codex] For each deferred check, record the repository, check/command, affected packages
[codex] or configurations, observed failure or reason not attempted, and the Phase 12
[codex] operator action and expected proof. Sibling phases keep this handoff in their
[codex] own docs and link here; Phase 12 consolidates it in the coverage report.
[codex] 
[codex] The Phase 12 operator sequence is:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex]    free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex]    Maven lookup within its job limits. Complete this before publication can
[codex]    trigger any prepared push workflows.
[codex] 2. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex]    consumer configurations.
[codex] 3. Manually dispatch
[codex]    `dependency-automation-config.yml` with `run_hosted_dry_run` enabled. Its
[codex]    GitHub-provided job token has read permissions only, Renovate runs with
[codex]    `--dry-run=full`, and the user retains control of the trigger. Preserve the
[codex]    workflow URL and confirm that the published preset resolves before proceeding;
[codex]    never copy the job token into an agent environment.
[codex] 4. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex]    rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] 5. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex]    updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] 6. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex]    and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex]    expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] 7. Run each Java repository's graph-submission workflow on its trusted default
[codex]    branch using its existing scoped package-read secrets and a separate GitHub
[codex]    job token for submission. Verify complete application/runtime/test dependency
[codex]    coverage and GitHub acceptance for every repo. A successful ordinary build,
[codex]    package-access preflight, or partial snapshot is insufficient. Preserve a
[codex]    sanitized snapshot or equivalent detailed graph evidence with the run URL and
[codex]    source revision; the orchestration-only Renovate dry run does not prove Maven
[codex]    resolution or Java submission. Resolve every other deferred authenticated
[codex]    lookup/build/scan and retain its evidence too.
[codex] 8. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex]    extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex]    message before enabling consumers.
[codex] 9. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex]    false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex]    and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] 
[codex] The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Local validation and dry run
[codex] 
[codex] The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] `renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] `renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] Use debug logging and do not provide a GitHub token or enable a write-capable
[codex] platform mode. Local mode proves extraction and supported lookups but does not
[codex] perform a true full dry run. Phase 12 owns the post-publication GitHub-platform
[codex] full dry run through the manually dispatched, read-only workflow; its ephemeral
[codex] job token is never provided to an agent.
[codex] 
[codex] Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] [`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] `deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] 
[codex] Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] 
[codex] - the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] - the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] - a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] - a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] - Trivy CLI/database and registry-resolver metadata, database-download logs,
[codex]   and a machine-readable completion status
[codex] 
[codex] A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] `ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] The cert-manager controller/startup refs and Istio CNI/pilot refs are likewise
[codex] tag-only chart output; only their resolved artifact for a particular run is
[codex] exact. The cert-manager ACME solver input does retain its checked-in digest.
[codex] 
[codex] The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] `guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] target as a known unscannable gap rather than adding a live-cluster dependency
[codex] or claiming coverage. Unexpected render, resolution, database, or scan failures
[codex] still fail the job.
[codex] 
[codex] Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] package scan.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access through the Phase 12 operator handoff. During Phases 1–11,
[codex]   record authentication-dependent checks as pending and continue independent local
[codex]   work. Never seek credentials in the agent environment, use Maven Local as proof
[codex]   of remote resolution, drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error. A
[codex]   resolution defect unrelated to authentication still needs investigation.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] [codex] ## Custom System Prompt
[codex] [codex] 
[codex] [codex] Using `claude-with-custom-system-prompt` is optional. The standard `claude` command and the inspection-only `claude-with-proxy` flow are fine for normal development.
[codex] [codex] 
[codex] [codex] This custom launcher exists because Claude Code's `--system-prompt` flags append to Anthropic's default system prompt instead of replacing it. The mitmproxy addon in `ai-agent-sandbox/system-prompt-addon.py` swaps only the main prompt body in flight and preserves the required prefix blocks. The custom prompt text lives in `ai-agent-sandbox/system-prompt.md`.
[codex] [codex] 
[codex] [codex] Read those files before changing prompt replacement behavior. Use `claude-with-proxy` when you only need traffic inspection. Use `claude-with-custom-system-prompt` when you specifically want the lean prompt behavior as part of the test or workflow.
[codex] [codex] 
[codex] [codex] ## Operating Rules
[codex] [codex] 
[codex] [codex] - Keep all work products inside this repository. Do not install, copy, or move files into system paths except by explicitly invoking the workspace-owned `ensure-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust` command for its exact local target.
[codex] [codex] - When you need to test a file that originates in `ai-agent-sandbox/`, copy it into `tmp/` and test from there.
[codex] [codex] - Redirect Python bytecode from sandbox-derived validation into `tmp/pycache`, for example: `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=tmp/pycache python3 -m py_compile &lt;file>`.
[codex] [codex] - Stop and report missing tools, credentials, or environment prerequisites instead of inventing workarounds.
[codex] [codex] - Do not treat archived or plan-oriented docs as active implementation authority unless the user explicitly asks for that context.
[codex] [codex] - Before live work against exactly `https://app.budgetanalyzer.localhost`, or after a certificate-chain failure for that origin, run `ensure-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust`. Use `check-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust` for read-only diagnosis.
[codex] [codex] - If the host publication is missing, stop and ask the user to run orchestration `./setup.sh` on the host. Never generate or rotate browser-facing certificates in the container.
[codex] [codex] - Never use HTTP, `--insecure`, `verify=False`, or `ignore_https_errors` to bypass a local trust failure. Do not run the lazy trust command for staging, production, arbitrary origins, or non-certificate failures.

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Local configuration is prepared; automation is not active.
[codex] 
[codex] The Budget Analyzer
[codex] [dependency automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] owns activation, scheduling, review, and cost boundaries. Renovate is the only
[codex] update-PR owner. Dependabot remains alert-only, and neither routine nor security
[codex] updates are automerged.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Native Renovate managers
[codex] cover the Go directive and direct and indirect modules in `go.mod`, both pinned
[codex] Dockerfile images, and GitHub Actions. A repository-specific regex manager covers
[codex] the `GOVULNCHECK_VERSION` value in
[codex] `.github/workflows/go-vulnerability-check.yml` as the Go module
[codex] `golang.org/x/vuln`.
[codex] 
[codex] The existing `build.yml` workflow remains the pull-request check for formatting,
[codex] tests, and the service image build. Dependency automation does not bypass those
[codex] checks. The shared preset must be published before this consumer configuration is
[codex] activated. This onboarding does not update `go.mod`, `go.sum`, the Go directive,
[codex] container images, Actions, or application code.
[codex] 
[codex] A credential-free local run with Renovate 44.65.5 under Node 24 extracted 21
[codex] occurrences from six files: two Dockerfile dependencies, 14 GitHub
[codex] Actions/runner/Go inputs, four `go.mod` entries, and one regex-managed scanner
[codex] pin. The module entries were `go`, `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9`,
[codex] `github.com/cespare/xxhash/v2`, and `github.com/dgryski/go-rendezvous`. Renovate
[codex] recognizes the latter two as indirect and leaves their standalone updates
[codex] disabled; they remain represented in the module graph and can change through a
[codex] reviewed direct-module update.
[codex] 
[codex] The local lookup independently found go-redis 9.7.3 as the maintained-line patch
[codex] and exposed later v9 release lines through 9.22.0. It also resolved the
[codex] distroless runtime image and the current scanner module. The Go builder image was
[codex] extracted, but Renovate's anonymous Docker Hub client returned `no-result` and an
[codex] anonymous Docker-token warning. GitHub Actions and the workflow's Go 1.26.x input
[codex] were extracted but skipped because no GitHub token was supplied. These incomplete
[codex] lookups are retained for the hosted Phase 12 retry. Extraction completed without
[codex] an exception or fatal log; its only error-level entry was the documented
[codex] missing-GitHub-token condition.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Reachable vulnerability evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `go-vulnerability-check.yml` runs after changes reach `main`, every Monday, and
[codex] on manual dispatch. It installs the pinned official `govulncheck` CLI and runs
[codex] both `govulncheck ./...` and `govulncheck -json ./...`. The workflow keeps the
[codex] readable report, JSON event stream, stderr, scanner version, and exit-code summary
[codex] for seven days.
[codex] 
[codex] Reachable findings are reported and uploaded without failing unrelated work.
[codex] Scanner installation, package loading, vulnerability database access, analysis,
[codex] JSON generation or validation, empty required evidence, and artifact upload
[codex] failures still fail the job. In particular, the text command's exit code 3 means
[codex] findings, while any other unexpected text status or any nonzero JSON status is an
[codex] operational error.
[codex] 
[codex] The application still declares Go 1.24. The current pinned scanner,
[codex] `golang.org/x/vuln` v1.7.0, requires Go 1.25 or newer, so this workflow uses Go
[codex] 1.26.x solely as its analysis toolchain and sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` to prevent an
[codex] implicit toolchain change. That does not upgrade the application toolchain or its
[codex] builder image.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Local baseline evidence
[codex] 
[codex] On 2026-09-06, govulncheck v1.7.0 running with Go 1.26.8 reproduced
[codex] GO-2025-3540 as a reachable vulnerability in
[codex] `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` 9.7.0. The fixed version reported by the scanner is
[codex] 9.7.3. A representative trace is:
[codex] 
[codex] ```text
[codex] session.go:81:24: ext.NewSessionStore calls redis.cmdable.Ping,
[codex] which eventually calls redis.baseClient.initConn
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] The scanner reported one reachable vulnerability from one module and no other
[codex] vulnerabilities in imported packages or required modules. This call-path result
[codex] is stronger evidence than module presence alone and reproduces the preserved
[codex] September 6 review. No remediation upgrade is part of this onboarding phase.
[codex] 
[codex] Run the same local check with an explicit analysis toolchain and pinned scanner:
[codex]

[codex] scan_output="$(mktemp -d)"

[codex] The explicit local analysis toolchain may download that public Go release when
[codex] it is not cached. It does not alter `go.mod` or the Dockerfile builder version.

[codex] ## Phase 1 pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.
[codex]

[codex] occurrences across 35 package files. The new workflow contributed six native
[codex] GitHub Actions records: checkout, pinned yq, pinned Trivy setup, pinned Trivy
[codex] CLI input, artifact upload, and the runner identity. The native manager owns all
[codex] of them; no scanner-specific custom manager was needed.

[codex] The offline render and YAML extraction path produced 32 distinct
[codex] image/platform targets from checked-in sources: 28 production/controller refs
[codex] for `linux/arm64`, three local-only refs for `linux/amd64`, and the Istio gateway
[codex] chart's unresolved `image: auto` marker. The workflow scans each registry ref
[codex] only after resolving the platform child digest. The `auto` marker is explicitly
[codex] unscannable without the live Istio injector, so the workflow retains it as a
[codex] known gap without turning that expected limitation into a scan error. Unexpected
[codex] render, resolution, database, and Trivy failures do fail. The render included
[codex] controller hooks, the cert-manager solver argument, the Prometheus
[codex] config-reloader argument, and all five explicit monitoring image overrides.

[codex]             > dependency-audit-reports/npm-audit-production.json \

[codex] 
[codex]           audit_operational_failure=0

[codex]           classify_audit() {

[codex]             report="$2"
[codex]             command_status="$3"
[codex] 
[codex]             if [[ ! -s "${report}" ]]; then
[codex]               echo "${scope} npm audit produced no JSON report." >&2
[codex]               audit_operational_failure=1
[codex]               return
[codex]             fi
[codex] 
[codex]             if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "${report}" > /dev/null; then
[codex]               echo "${scope} npm audit produced invalid JSON." >&2
[codex]               audit_operational_failure=1
[codex]               return
[codex]             fi

[codex]               || [[ "${command_status}" -ne 0 && "${command_status}" -ne 1 ]]; then

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Local configuration and audit workflow prepared; automation is not
[codex] installed or active. Authenticated acceptance is pending the system-wide
[codex] activation phase.
[codex] 
[codex] This repository uses Renovate as the sole owner of dependency-update pull
[codex] requests. GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts provide alert-only
[codex] vulnerability evidence; Dependabot version-update and security-update pull
[codex] requests must remain disabled. The shared operating policy is owned by the
[codex] [orchestration dependency-automation guide](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md).
[codex] 
[codex] ## Update discovery
[codex] 
[codex] `renovate.json` extends the Budget Analyzer shared preset. Renovate discovers:
[codex] 
[codex] - direct npm dependencies and lockfile selections from `package.json` and
[codex]   `package-lock.json`;
[codex] - Node and NGINX build/runtime images, tags, and digests in all three
[codex]   Dockerfiles;
[codex] - pinned GitHub Actions and `actions/setup-node` runtime inputs in the workflow
[codex]   files.
[codex] 
[codex] Routine updates and lockfile maintenance run on the shared weekly schedule.
[codex] React and React DOM updates are grouped, as are the Vitest runner, UI, and
[codex] coverage packages. The shared policy disables automerge, keeps patch, minor,
[codex] and major proposals distinguishable, and requires Dependency Dashboard approval
[codex] for majors. Toolchain majors such as TypeScript, Vite, Vitest, ESLint, Tailwind,
[codex] React Router, and Node therefore remain visible for compatibility review rather
[codex] than being excluded or constrained to historical target versions.
[codex] 
[codex] Lockfile maintenance is discovery work, not permission to run `npm audit fix` or
[codex] silently refresh the checked-in lockfile during onboarding. Review dependency
[codex] and lockfile diffs together. For image updates, retain immutable digests and
[codex] verify the selected tag/digest supports the required platform before merging.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Audit evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `.github/workflows/dependency-audit.yml` runs weekly and on manual dispatch. It
[codex] installs exactly `package-lock.json` with `npm ci`, then independently captures:
[codex] 
[codex] - `npm audit --json` as `npm-audit-full.json`;
[codex] - `npm audit --omit=dev --json` as `npm-audit-production.json`.
[codex] 
[codex] Download the `npm-audit-reports` artifact from the workflow run to compare the
[codex] raw JSON reports. The artifact is retained for seven days and also includes each
[codex] command's stderr and `status.txt`. The job summary presents severity counts for
[codex] the two scopes.
[codex] 
[codex] An npm audit exit status caused by findings does not fail this scheduled report;
[codex] the existing backlog remains visible without blocking unrelated pull requests.
[codex] Missing or malformed JSON, an npm-reported registry error, an unexpected command
[codex] status, or an `npm ci` failure does fail the workflow. Installation errors remain
[codex] separate in the named install step's log, while audit errors and partial report
[codex] files remain available through the always-upload artifact step.
[codex] 
[codex] The credential-free onboarding run on 2026-09-06 reproduced the saved review
[codex] against the unchanged lockfile:
[codex] 
[codex] | Scope                   | Critical | High | Moderate | Low | Total | Top-level vulnerable paths                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
[codex] | ----------------------- | -------: | ---: | -------: | --: | ----: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
[codex] | Full dependency tree    |        3 |   13 |        2 |   2 |    20 | `@babel/core`, `@humanfs/node`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `@vitest/ui`, `axios`, `brace-expansion`, `browserslist`, `fflate`, `flatted`, `form-data`, `js-yaml`, `nanoid`, `picomatch`, `postcss`, `postcss-selector-parser`, `react-router`, `react-router-dom`, `vite`, `vitest`, `ws` |
[codex] | Production dependencies |        0 |    4 |        0 |   0 |     4 | `axios`, `form-data`, `react-router`, `react-router-dom`                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
[codex] 
[codex] Both commands returned status 1 because findings exist, produced valid
[codex] vulnerability metadata, and reported no registry error. Compare advisory and
[codex] package identities in future runs rather than relying on the historical total:
[codex] new advisories can appear while old ones are remediated.
[codex] 
[codex] Reachability and runtime applicability remain human triage. In particular,
[codex] development-server findings are not production-browser findings, and this SPA
[codex] does not use React Server Components or React Router's server/framework modes.
[codex] Those distinctions inform priority but do not justify dropping findings from the
[codex] full report.
[codex]

[codex] ## Bot pull request checks
[codex] 
[codex] Every Renovate pull request remains non-automerged. The existing `Build`
[codex] pull-request workflow runs locked installation, ESLint, the Vitest coverage gate,
[codex] the production-smoke CSP gate, and the standard TypeScript/Vite bundle. Reviewers
[codex] must also inspect release notes, the resolved lockfile change, browser and SSR/RSC
[codex] applicability, strict-CSP behavior, and Node/image platform compatibility.
[codex] 
[codex] The [development guide](development.md#repository-commands) owns local build and
[codex] validation commands. CSP-sensitive dependency changes must also follow the
[codex] [architecture CSP contract](architecture.md#content-security-policy) and the
[codex] [external browser harness](testing-guide.md#external-browser-harness); the bot
[codex] cannot infer runtime stylesheet injection or mobile/browser compatibility from
[codex] a successful package lookup.

[codex] function getSystemArchitecture(useSystem) {
[codex] 	if (!useSystem) return null;
[codex] 	switch (process.arch) {
[codex] 		case "ia32": return "x86";
[codex] 		case "arm64": return "aarch64";
[codex] 		case "arm":
[codex] 		case "riscv64":
[codex] 		case "s390x":
[codex] 		case "x64": return process.arch;
[codex] 		default:
[codex] 			logger.warn({ arch: process.arch }, "Unknown system architecture, defaulting to null");
[codex] 			return null;
[codex] 	}
[codex] }
[codex] function getSystemOs(useSystem) {
[codex] 	if (!useSystem) return null;
[codex] 	switch (process.platform) {
[codex] 		case "darwin": return "mac";
[codex] 		case "win32": return "windows";
[codex] 		case "aix":
[codex] 		case "linux": return process.platform;
[codex] 		default:
[codex] 			logger.warn({ os: process.platform }, "Unknown system OS, defaulting to null");
[codex] 			return null;
[codex] 	}
[codex] }

[codex] const adoptiumRegistryUrl = "https://api.adoptium.net/";
[codex] async function getPageReleases(http, url, page) {
[codex] 	const pgUrl = `${url}&page=${page}`;
[codex] 	try {
[codex] 		return (await http.getJson(pgUrl, AdoptiumJavaResponse))?.body?.versions?.map(({ semver }) => ({ version: semver })) ?? null;
[codex] 	} catch (err) {
[codex] 		if (page !== 0 && err instanceof RequestError && err.response?.statusCode === 404) return null;
[codex] 		throw err;
[codex] 	}
[codex] }
[codex] async function getAdoptiumReleases(http, pkgConfig) {
[codex] 	logger.trace({ pkgConfig }, "fetching Adoptium releases");
[codex] 	let url = `${adoptiumRegistryUrl}v3/info/release_versions?page_size=50&image_type=${pkgConfig.imageType}&project=jdk&release_type=ga&sort_method=DATE&sort_order=DESC`;
[codex] 	if (pkgConfig.architecture) url += `&architecture=${pkgConfig.architecture}`;
[codex] 	if (pkgConfig.os) url += `&os=${pkgConfig.os}`;
[codex] 	const result = {
[codex] 		homepage: "https://adoptium.net",
[codex] 		releases: []
[codex] 	};
[codex] 	try {
[codex] 		let page = 0;
[codex] 		let releases = await getPageReleases(http, url, page);
[codex] 		while (releases) {
[codex] 			result.releases.push(...releases);
[codex] 			if (releases.length !== 50 || page >= 50) break;
[codex] 			page += 1;
[codex] 			releases = await getPageReleases(http, url, page);
[codex] 		}
[codex] 	} catch (err) {
[codex] 		if (err instanceof RequestError) {
[codex] 			if (err.response?.statusCode !== 404) throw new ExternalHostError(err);
[codex] 			return null;
[codex] 		}
[codex] 		throw err;
[codex] 	}
[codex] 	return result.releases.length ? result : null;
[codex] }

[codex] # AGENTS.md Checkstyle
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Active
[codex] **Purpose:** Provide reusable rules for writing `AGENTS.md` files that help
[codex] AI coding agents work safely and accurately without creating documentation
[codex] drift.
[codex] 
[codex] Use this document as a public reference when creating or reviewing an
[codex] `AGENTS.md` file in any repository:
[codex] 
[codex] ```text
[codex] Inspect this repository and generate an AGENTS.md file using the guidelines in
[codex] budgetanalyzer/orchestration/docs/agents-md-checkstyle.md.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] For remote use, point agents at:
[codex] https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/agents-md-checkstyle.md
[codex] 
[codex] ## Core Standard
[codex] 
[codex] An `AGENTS.md` file is an operating contract for coding agents. It should teach
[codex] the agent how to work in the repository, where to find current truth, what it
[codex] may change, what it must not change, and how to verify work.
[codex] 
[codex] It should not become a stale inventory of services, classes, endpoints, ports,
[codex] dependency versions, or setup steps that already have a closer source of truth.
[codex] 
[codex] The durable pattern is:
[codex] 
[codex] ```text
[codex] Stable rule + discovery command + source-of-truth pointer
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Prefer this:
[codex] 
[codex] ````markdown
[codex] Service manifests live under kubernetes/services/. Discover them with:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] find kubernetes/services -maxdepth 2 -type f | sort
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Exact ports and exposure rules live in docs/architecture/port-reference.md.
[codex] ````
[codex] 
[codex] Avoid this:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] Services:
[codex] - transaction-service on port 8082
[codex] - currency-service on port 8084
[codex] - permission-service on port 8086
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] The first form survives refactoring. The second form drifts.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Preservation Rule
[codex] 
[codex] When tightening or refactoring an existing `AGENTS.md`, preserve unique
[codex] information. Do not remove a rule, guardrail, workflow, boundary, or operating
[codex] constraint unless one of these is true:
[codex] 
[codex] - The same meaning is preserved in the rewritten `AGENTS.md`.
[codex] - The information is moved to a clearly named, closer source-of-truth document
[codex]   and `AGENTS.md` now points to it.
[codex] - The rule is genuinely obsolete for the current repository, and the rewrite
[codex]   says so intentionally rather than deleting it silently.
[codex] 
[codex] Treat deletion as the last option, not the default cleanup action.
[codex] 
[codex] Do not equate "shorter" with "better." If a section contains non-duplicated
[codex] repo-specific guidance, keep it or re-home it before removing it.
[codex] 
[codex] Example:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] Keep this kind of direct guardrail if no closer owner doc exists:
[codex] 
[codex] ## Git Safety
[codex] 
[codex] Never run git write commands such as `commit`, `push`, `checkout`, `reset`, or
[codex] branch manipulation unless explicitly requested.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] If you replace a concrete section with a pointer, verify the pointer actually
[codex] owns the full instruction. Do not replace unique guidance with an empty link.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Consultation Trigger Pattern
[codex] 
[codex] Important pointers should explain when an agent should read the referenced
[codex] file. A path alone says where detail exists; a consultation trigger tells the
[codex] agent when to spend context on that detail.
[codex] 
[codex] The trigger does not need to be a literal `When to consult` block. It can be an
[codex] inline rule, a section-level bullet list, or a short imperative sentence. Use
[codex] the block form when several related triggers need to be grouped together.
[codex] 
[codex] Use this pattern for source-of-truth docs, config files, runbooks, generated
[codex] artifacts, and decision records:
[codex] 
[codex] ```text
[codex] Topic summary:
[codex] - Stable rule or short orientation.
[codex] - Current details live in &lt;path>.
[codex] - Trigger: read &lt;path> when &lt;specific task or failure mode applies>.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Good forms:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] Before writing or modifying Java code, read
[codex] docs/code-quality-standards.md. Do not skip this step.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] For comprehensive testing strategies, read docs/testing-patterns.md when
[codex] writing tests.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] API routes are resource-based and should stay decoupled from service names.
[codex] Current gateway routes live in nginx/nginx.k8s.conf.
[codex] 
[codex] When to consult nginx/nginx.k8s.conf:
[codex] - Adding or changing a public `/api/...` route.
[codex] - Debugging a request that reaches the SPA instead of a backend.
[codex] - Verifying local and production gateway parity.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Avoid this:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] See nginx/nginx.k8s.conf for routes.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Good triggers are action-oriented:
[codex] 
[codex] - Before changing setup, read the getting-started or bootstrap docs.
[codex] - Before changing public APIs, read OpenAPI specs and route ownership docs.
[codex] - Before changing deployment, read manifests, overlays, and deployment runbooks.
[codex] - Before changing architecture or ownership, read the relevant ADRs and active
[codex]   architecture docs.
[codex] - When a verifier fails, read the focused troubleshooting runbook before
[codex]   inventing a workaround.
[codex] 
[codex] Do not add consultation triggers mechanically for every link. Use them for
[codex] references where timing matters or where agents are likely to guess instead of
[codex] loading the owner doc.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Imperative Language
[codex] 
[codex] Write agent instructions as direct operating rules, not passive descriptions.
[codex] Agents follow clear commands better than background prose.
[codex] 
[codex] Prefer imperative forms:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] Before writing or modifying Java code, read docs/code-quality-standards.md.
[codex] Run `./gradlew test` before finishing Java changes.
[codex] Do not edit generated files directly.
[codex] Stop and report missing prerequisites instead of inventing workarounds.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Avoid descriptive forms that leave the action implicit:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] The code-quality standards document contains Java style guidance.
[codex] Tests are available through Gradle.
[codex] Generated files are usually produced by the build.
[codex] Prerequisites may be required.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Use `must`, `never`, `always`, `do not`, `before`, `after`, and `when` where
[codex] the rule is mandatory. Use `prefer` where the guidance is a default with
[codex] legitimate exceptions.
[codex] 
[codex] Do not make every sentence forceful. Repository purpose, architecture summaries,
[codex] and source-of-truth descriptions can be explanatory. Guardrails, workflows,
[codex] validation gates, and consultation triggers should be imperative.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Rule Set
[codex] 
[codex] | ID | Rule | Check |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | AG001 | Prefer patterns over inventories. | If adding a list of concrete services, classes, endpoints, ports, or versions, ask whether a command or owner doc can reveal it instead. |
[codex] | AG002 | Point to the closest source of truth. | Link to config, manifests, README files, runbooks, OpenAPI specs, package files, or build files instead of copying their exact detail. |
[codex] | AG003 | Include discovery commands. | Give `rg`, `find`, `tree`, package-manager, runtime, or framework commands that reveal current state. |
[codex] | AG004 | Keep stable guardrails directly in `AGENTS.md`. | Include write boundaries, destructive-command policy, security constraints, validation requirements, and workflow rules that agents must always see. |
[codex] | AG005 | Keep volatile details out of `AGENTS.md`. | Do not duplicate full setup flows, generated route maps, dependency tables, class inventories, or API contracts. |
[codex] | AG006 | Make repository authority explicit. | State the repo role, scope, read/write permissions, related repos, and ownership boundaries. |
[codex] | AG007 | Use prerequisite-first workflows. | Tell agents to check required tools, environment, credentials, and repo-owned setup docs before implementing work. |
[codex] | AG008 | Define verification gates. | Name the tests, linters, smoke checks, scripts, or manual checks expected before work is complete. |
[codex] | AG009 | Keep paths portable. | Use relative paths or repo-root-relative paths. Avoid machine-specific absolute paths. |
[codex] | AG010 | Avoid eager file imports unless intended. | Use plain text paths (`docs/file.md`) or markdown links (`[docs/file.md](docs/file.md)`). In Claude-oriented files, avoid `@path` syntax, which pre-loads content at startup. |
[codex] | AG011 | Use hierarchy intentionally. | Put global rules at the repo root and place subtree-specific `AGENTS.md` files near specialized code only when the agent tooling supports hierarchical context. |
[codex] | AG012 | Keep active docs separate from history. | Point to active owner docs for implementation work. Mark archives and decision records as context unless they are intentionally active surfaces. |
[codex] | AG013 | Preserve useful direct context. | Do not shrink `AGENTS.md` into a bare index. Keep enough high-signal rules for agents to act without rediscovering basic operating constraints. |
[codex] | AG014 | Make missing prerequisites explicit. | Tell agents to stop and report missing required tools or environment state rather than inventing workarounds. |
[codex] | AG015 | Explain when to update `AGENTS.md`. | Update it for new instructions, guardrails, workflows, or discovery commands, not for every ordinary code or config change. |
[codex] | AG016 | Add consultation triggers for important references. | For key docs and config pointers, name the concrete tasks or failure modes that should trigger reading them. Inline guidance is fine; a literal `When to consult` block is optional. |
[codex] | AG017 | Use imperative language for agent actions. | Write guardrails, workflows, validation gates, and consultation triggers as direct commands. Avoid passive descriptions when action is required. |
[codex] | AG018 | Re-home unique guidance before removing it. | Do not delete repo-specific instructions just to reduce length. Preserve them in `AGENTS.md`, or move them to a real owner doc and leave a pointer. |
[codex] 
[codex] ## Recommended Structure
[codex] 
[codex] Use the sections that fit the repository. Rename them if local terminology is
[codex] clearer, but keep the same intent.
[codex] 
[codex] ### 1. Repository Position
[codex] 
[codex] State what the repo is and what authority it has.
[codex] 
[codex] Include:
[codex] 
[codex] - Archetype, such as application, library, service, orchestration, tooling, or
[codex]   documentation.
[codex] - Scope, such as one service, one package, a monorepo area, or a whole
[codex]   ecosystem.
[codex] - Relationships to sibling repos, generated artifacts, deployment repos, or
[codex]   shared libraries.
[codex] - Read and write boundaries for agents.
[codex] 
[codex] Example:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] ## Repository Position
[codex] 
[codex] **Archetype:** service
[codex] **Scope:** payments API
[codex] **Role:** owns payment authorization and capture workflows
[codex] 
[codex] ### Boundaries
[codex] - Read shared contracts from ../service-common.
[codex] - Write application code, tests, and docs in this repo.
[codex] - Do not change deployment manifests in ../orchestration from this context.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ### 2. Discovery
[codex] 
[codex] Give commands that reveal current structure and runtime state. Discovery
[codex] commands are better than static inventories because they remain accurate when
[codex] the repository changes.
[codex] 
[codex] Common examples:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] # Repo structure
[codex] find . -maxdepth 2 -type f | sort
[codex] tree -L 2 -I 'node_modules|target|build|dist|.git'
[codex] 
[codex] # Text and symbol search
[codex] rg -n "pattern"
[codex] rg --files
[codex] 
[codex] # Build tool state
[codex] ./gradlew tasks
[codex] npm run
[codex] go test ./...
[codex] 
[codex] # Runtime state
[codex] docker compose ps
[codex] kubectl get pods -A
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Only include commands that are relevant to the repo and likely to work in a
[codex] normal development environment.
[codex] 
[codex] ### 3. Source Of Truth
[codex] 
[codex] Name canonical docs and files by topic. This lets `AGENTS.md` summarize without
[codex] copying. For high-value references, include consultation triggers so the agent
[codex] knows when to load the owner doc.
[codex] 
[codex] Good source-of-truth pointers include:
[codex] 
[codex] - Setup and onboarding docs.
[codex] - Architecture docs.
[codex] - API specs.
[codex] - Build files and dependency catalogs.
[codex] - Runtime manifests.
[codex] - Script catalogs.
[codex] - Runbooks.
[codex] - Security policy docs.
[codex] - ADRs for decision rationale.
[codex] 
[codex] Example:
[codex] 
[codex] ```markdown
[codex] ## Source Of Truth
[codex] 
[codex] - Local setup: docs/development/getting-started.md
[codex] - API contract: docs/api/openapi.yaml
[codex] - Build and dependency rules: build.gradle.kts and gradle/libs.versions.toml
[codex] - Deployment manifests: ../orchestration/kubernetes/services/payments/
[codex] - Operational runbooks: docs/runbooks/
[codex] 
[codex] Consultation triggers:
[codex] - Setup docs: before changing prerequisites, bootstrap, or local run behavior.
[codex] - API contracts: before adding, removing, or reshaping endpoints.
[codex] - Deployment manifests: before changing probes, ports, resources, or service
[codex]   wiring.
[codex] - Runbooks: when reproducing or debugging an operational failure.
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ### 4. Operating Rules
[codex] 
[codex] Put stable constraints directly in `AGENTS.md`. Agents should not have to hunt
[codex] for rules that prevent unsafe or invalid changes.
[codex] 
[codex] Common operating rules:
[codex] 
[codex] - Never run destructive git commands unless explicitly requested.
[codex] - Do not commit, push, reset, or rewrite history unless explicitly requested.
[codex] - Do not write outside the allowed repository or owned subtree.
[codex] - Do not edit generated files directly unless the generator is unavailable and
[codex]   the limitation is documented.
[codex] - Do not bypass security, auth, policy, persistence, or validation layers as a
[codex]   durable fix.
[codex] - Treat manual live-environment changes as diagnostics unless they are encoded
[codex]   back into repo-owned config.
[codex] name: Exact Image Security Evidence
[codex] 
[codex] on:
[codex]   schedule:
[codex]     - cron: '23 4 * * 6'
[codex]   workflow_dispatch:
[codex] 
[codex] permissions:
[codex]   contents: read
[codex]

[codex]   group: exact-image-security-evidence
[codex]   cancel-in-progress: false

[codex]   TRIVY_CACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/scan-work/trivy-cache

[codex]       - name: Extract rendered image references
[codex]         uses: mikefarah/yq@e1d5d6eb36b8995bf29e5acb561659824dc47be3 # v4.53.6
[codex]         with:
[codex]           cmd: |
[codex]             set -eu
[codex]             : > scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex]             for platform_dir in scan-work/rendered/linux-*; do

[codex]               for manifest in "${platform_dir}"/*.yaml; do

[codex]                   (
[codex]                     .. | select(tag == "!!map") | .image? |
[codex]                     select(tag == "!!str")
[codex]                   ),

[codex]                     ) |

[codex]                   )

[codex]                 while IFS= read -r image_ref; do

[codex]                     ghcr.io/budgetanalyzer/*) continue ;;
[codex]                   esac

[codex]                 done &lt; scan-work/extracted-image-refs.txt
[codex]               done
[codex]             done

[codex] 
[codex]       - name: Build the deduplicated scan target manifest

[codex]           jq -Rn '
[codex]             [
[codex]               inputs |

[codex]             ] |
[codex]             group_by([.platform, .source_ref]) |
[codex]             map({
[codex]               platform: .[0].platform,
[codex]               source_ref: .[0].source_ref,
[codex]               sources: (map(.source) | unique)
[codex]             })

[codex]           test "$(jq 'length' scan-work/targets.json)" -gt 0
[codex]           {

[codex]           } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node and Zulu package versions when Trivy
[codex] +   exposes them. It records the declared Go archive and retains any discoverable
[codex] +   Go files/packages without claiming that declaration alone proves the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=1000 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=1000 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. The local build/Trivy validation record
[codex] +below is updated only from an actual no-cache build and raw scanner output; a
[codex] +successful base-index check alone does not establish installed-package evidence.
[codex] +

[codex] +  extracted, Ubuntu 24.04 digest proposals preserve digest-only syntax, and no

[codex] +  need that hosted context.
[codex] +- Repository: `budgetanalyzer/workspace`. Check: Actions cost and hosted image

[codex] +  build, Node/Zulu inventory, Go declaration/discovery result, and successful
[codex] +  Trivy database and scan statuses. Stop for user direction if this requires
[codex] +  spend.

[codex] +  assets, PyPI/npm, Playwright, and Trivy databases. Reason: local public success
[codex] +  does not prove the hosted network path, and no registry login is requested

[codex] +  preserve sanitized settings and alert evidence for the final cross-repository
[codex] +  coverage report.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate and Trivy do not establish lifecycle support. Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu,
[codex] +Kubernetes, Helm, Kind, and other installed tools remain subject to the
[codex] +quarterly human upstream-support review owned by the shared policy.
