[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] +Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex] +   Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex] +   the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] +at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] +by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] +that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] +than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. A no-cache local `linux/amd64` build from
[codex] +the Compose context completed on 2026-09-07 without starting or pushing the
[codex] +image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] +`24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local
[codex] +evidence is staged under `tmp/dependency-automation/local-image-scan/`; it is
[codex] +temporary validation output rather than a checked-in report. Vulnerability
[codex] +findings were reported, while scanner and database operations completed; the
[codex] +existing backlog remains non-gating under the shared policy.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records
[codex] +from 13 files: one Dev Container feature, one native digest-only Dockerfile
[codex] +record, five workflow records, and nine regex-managed Dockerfile records. The
[codex] +safe Ubuntu manager separately proposed the current 24.04 digest and a visible
[codex] +26.04 major; its replacement preserves the digest-only form. Node 24 was current,
[codex] +the Go source exposed maintained-line 1.24 and later lines, and PyPI exposed a
[codex] +mitmproxy patch. The safe Ubuntu Docker lookup succeeded. GitHub-backed identities
[codex] +were extracted but reported `github-token-required`; those lookups remain pending
[codex] +Phase 12 rather than being reported as successful.
[codex] +

[codex] @@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] +Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex] +   Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex] +   the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] +at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] +by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] +that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] +than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. A no-cache local `linux/amd64` build from
[codex] +the Compose context completed on 2026-09-07 without starting or pushing the
[codex] +image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] +`24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local
[codex] +evidence is staged under `tmp/dependency-automation/local-image-scan/`; it is
[codex] +temporary validation output rather than a checked-in report. Vulnerability
[codex] +scanning reported 4,381 result rows, including 29 critical and 767 high rows,
[codex] +while scanner and database operations completed. Counts include repeated Go
[codex] +standard-library findings across installed binaries and are not unique-advisory
[codex] +or review-parity totals. The existing backlog remains non-gating under the
[codex] +shared policy.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records
[codex] +from 13 files: one Dev Container feature, one native digest-only Dockerfile
[codex] +record, five workflow records, and nine regex-managed Dockerfile records. The
[codex] +safe Ubuntu manager separately proposed the current 24.04 digest and a visible
[codex] +26.04 major; its replacement preserves the digest-only form. Node 24 was current,
[codex] +the Go source exposed maintained-line 1.24 and later lines, and PyPI exposed a
[codex] +mitmproxy patch. The safe Ubuntu Docker lookup succeeded. GitHub-backed identities
[codex] +were extracted but reported `github-token-required`; those lookups remain pending
[codex] +Phase 12 rather than being reported as successful.
[codex] +

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] +Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex] +   Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex] +   the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] +at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] +by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] +that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] +than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. A no-cache local `linux/amd64` build from
[codex] +the Compose context completed on 2026-09-07 without starting or pushing the
[codex] +image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] +`24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local
[codex] +evidence is staged under `tmp/dependency-automation/local-image-scan/`; it is
[codex] +temporary validation output rather than a checked-in report. Vulnerability
[codex] +scanning reported 4,381 result rows, including 29 critical and 767 high rows,
[codex] +while scanner and database operations completed. Counts include repeated Go
[codex] +standard-library findings across installed binaries and are not unique-advisory
[codex] +or review-parity totals. The existing backlog remains non-gating under the
[codex] +shared policy.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records
[codex] +from 13 files: one Dev Container feature, one native digest-only Dockerfile
[codex] +record, five workflow records, and nine regex-managed Dockerfile records. The
[codex] +safe Ubuntu manager separately proposed the current 24.04 digest and a visible
[codex] +26.04 major; its replacement preserves the digest-only form. Node 24 was current,
[codex] +the Go source exposed maintained-line 1.24 and later lines, and PyPI exposed a
[codex] +mitmproxy patch. The safe Ubuntu Docker lookup succeeded. GitHub-backed identities
[codex] +were extracted but reported `github-token-required`; those lookups remain pending
[codex] +Phase 12 rather than being reported as successful.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Phase 12 operator handoff
[codex] +
[codex] +The following remains pending because preparation neither publishes files nor
[codex] +uses credentials or account settings:
[codex] +
[codex] +- Repository: `budgetanalyzer/workspace`. Check: hosted Renovate full dry run
[codex] +  after the shared preset and this consumer are published. Scope: the Ubuntu
[codex] +  digest-only mapping, Node, Go, kubectl, Helm, Tilt, mitmproxy, actionlint,
[codex] +  Kind, Dockerfile, and workflow Actions. Action: run the trusted read-only
[codex] +  hosted validation and then onboard the free Renovate App. Proof: retain the
[codex] +  run URL and logs showing the preset resolved, every declared identity was
[codex] +  extracted, Ubuntu 24.04 digest proposals preserve digest-only syntax, and no
[codex] +  fatal/error output occurred. GitHub-backed release lookups are expected to
[codex] +  need that hosted context.
[codex] +- Repository: `budgetanalyzer/workspace`. Check: Actions cost and hosted image
[codex] +  evidence. Scope: the three-hour-capable no-cache development-image build,
[codex] +  public image/package downloads, Trivy database, seven-day artifact, and
[codex] +  standard Linux runner. Action: before enabling the schedule, confirm repository
[codex] +  visibility, included Actions allowance, storage, and disabled paid overages;
[codex] +  then manually dispatch the workflow from trusted `main`. Proof: retain the run
[codex] +  URL, duration, source revision, artifact, exact base digest/index, complete
[codex] +  build, Node/Zulu inventory, Go declaration/discovery result, and successful
[codex] +  Trivy database and scan statuses. Stop for user direction if this requires
[codex] +  spend.
[codex] +- Repository: `budgetanalyzer/workspace`. Check: complete hosted public download
[codex] +  path. Scope: Docker Hub's Ubuntu index, NodeSource, Azul, Go, GitHub release
[codex] +  assets, PyPI/npm, Playwright, and Trivy databases. Reason: local public success
[codex] +  does not prove the hosted network path, and no registry login is requested
[codex] +  during preparation. Action: inspect strict hosted logs. Proof: every download
[codex] +  and scan completes without hidden authentication, rate-limit, or partial-data
[codex] +  failure; retain failures as gaps rather than adding credentials or bypasses.
[codex] +- Repository: `budgetanalyzer/workspace`. Check: GitHub dependency graph and
[codex] +  Dependabot alert settings. Action: enable the graph and alerts while keeping
[codex] +  Dependabot version and overlapping security-update PRs disabled. Proof:
[codex] +  preserve sanitized settings and alert evidence for the final cross-repository
[codex] +  coverage report.
[codex] +
[codex] +Renovate and Trivy do not establish lifecycle support. Node, Go, Java, Ubuntu,
[codex] +Kubernetes, Helm, Kind, and other installed tools remain subject to the
[codex] +quarterly human upstream-support review owned by the shared policy.

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] +Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex] +   Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex] +   the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] +at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] +by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] +that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] +than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. A no-cache local `linux/amd64` build from
[codex] +the Compose context completed on 2026-09-07 without starting or pushing the
[codex] +image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] +`24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local
[codex] +evidence is staged under `tmp/dependency-automation/local-image-scan/`; it is
[codex] +temporary validation output rather than a checked-in report. Vulnerability
[codex] +scanning reported 4,381 result rows, including 29 critical and 767 high rows,
[codex] +while scanner and database operations completed. Counts include repeated Go
[codex] +standard-library findings across installed binaries and are not unique-advisory
[codex] +or review-parity totals. The existing backlog remains non-gating under the
[codex] +shared policy.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records
[codex] +from 13 files: one Dev Container feature, one native digest-only Dockerfile
[codex] +record, five workflow records, and nine regex-managed Dockerfile records. The
[codex] +safe Ubuntu manager separately proposed the current 24.04 digest and a visible
[codex] +26.04 major; its replacement preserves the digest-only form. Node 24 was current,
[codex] +the Go source exposed maintained-line 1.24 and later lines, and PyPI exposed a
[codex] +mitmproxy patch. The safe Ubuntu Docker lookup succeeded. GitHub-backed identities
[codex] +were extracted but reported `github-token-required`; those lookups remain pending
[codex] +Phase 12 rather than being reported as successful.
[codex] +

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] +Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex] +   Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex] +   the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] +at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] +by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] +that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] +than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. A no-cache local `linux/amd64` build from
[codex] +the Compose context completed on 2026-09-07 without starting or pushing the
[codex] +image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] +`24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local
[codex] +evidence is staged under `tmp/dependency-automation/local-image-scan/`; it is
[codex] +temporary validation output rather than a checked-in report. Vulnerability
[codex] +scanning reported 4,381 result rows, including 29 critical and 767 high rows,
[codex] +while scanner and database operations completed. Counts include repeated Go
[codex] +standard-library findings across installed binaries and are not unique-advisory
[codex] +or review-parity totals. The existing backlog remains non-gating under the
[codex] +shared policy.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records
[codex] +from 13 files: one Dev Container feature, one native digest-only Dockerfile
[codex] +record, five workflow records, and nine regex-managed Dockerfile records. The
[codex] +safe Ubuntu manager separately proposed the current 24.04 digest and a visible
[codex] +26.04 major; its replacement preserves the digest-only form. Node 24 was current,
[codex] +the Go source exposed maintained-line 1.24 and later lines, and PyPI exposed a
[codex] +mitmproxy patch. The safe Ubuntu Docker lookup succeeded. GitHub-backed identities
[codex] +were extracted but reported `github-token-required`; those lookups remain pending
[codex] +Phase 12 rather than being reported as successful.
[codex] +

[codex] +            workspace-image-scan/base/imagetools-inspect.txt

[codex] +            --arg digest "${declared_digest}" \
[codex] +            --arg release_family "${expected_release}" \

[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] +Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex][codex] 
 +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex] +   Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex] +   the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] +at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] +by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] +that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] +than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. A no-cache local `linux/amd64` build from
[codex] +the Compose context completed on 2026-09-07 without starting or pushing the
[codex] +image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] +`24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local
[codex] +evidence is staged under `tmp/dependency-automation/local-image-scan/`; it is
[codex] +temporary validation output rather than a checked-in report. Vulnerability
[codex] +scanning reported 4,381 result rows, including 29 critical and 767 high rows,
[codex] +while scanner and database operations completed. Counts include repeated Go
[codex] +standard-library findings across installed binaries and are not unique-advisory
[codex] +or review-parity totals. The existing backlog remains non-gating under the
[codex] +shared policy.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records
[codex] +from 13 files: one Dev Container feature, one native digest-only Dockerfile
[codex] +record, five workflow records, and nine regex-managed Dockerfile records. The
[codex] +safe Ubuntu manager separately proposed the current 24.04 digest and a visible
[codex] +26.04 major; its replacement preserves the digest-only form. Node 24 was current,
[codex] +the Go source exposed maintained-line 1.24 and later lines, and PyPI exposed a
[codex] +mitmproxy patch. The safe Ubuntu Docker lookup succeeded. GitHub-backed identities
[codex] +were extracted but reported `github-token-required`; those lookups remain pending
[codex] +Phase 12 rather than being reported as successful.
[codex] +

[codex] @@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
[codex] +# Dependency Automation
[codex] +
[codex] +**Status:** Local configuration and image-scan workflow prepared; automation is
[codex] +not installed or active. Hosted acceptance is pending Phase 12.
[codex] +
[codex] +The shared
[codex] +[Budget Analyzer dependency-automation policy](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/orchestration/blob/main/docs/dependency-automation.md)
[codex] +owns scheduling, update-PR ownership, activation, cost, and failure handling.
[codex] +Renovate is the sole update-PR owner, automerge remains disabled, and Dependabot
[codex] +remains alert-only.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Update discovery
[codex] +
[codex] +`renovate.json` extends the shared orchestration preset. Renovate's native
[codex] +Dockerfile manager covers the workspace Dockerfile, while repository-specific
[codex] +regex managers identify version declarations embedded in ARGs and download
[codex] +URLs:
[codex] +
[codex] +| Source | Package identity | Representation and review boundary |
[codex] +| --- | --- | --- |
[codex] +| `NODE_MAJOR` | Node.js (`node-version`) | Major line only. NodeSource apt selects the current patch during a fresh build. |
[codex] +| `KUBECTL_VERSION` | `kubernetes/kubernetes` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `HELM_VERSION` | `helm/helm` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `TILT_VERSION` | `tilt-dev/tilt` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| `MITMPROXY_VERSION` | `mitmproxy` on PyPI | The pipx package is exactly pinned. |
[codex] +| `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` | `rhysd/actionlint` | Version is coupled to amd64 and arm64 SHA-256 values. |
[codex] +| Go archive URL | Go (`golang-version`) | Exact release, but the URL is hard-coded to `linux-amd64`. |
[codex] +| Kind download URL | `kubernetes-sigs/kind` | Exact release and TARGETARCH-aware URL, but the existing download has no checksum verification. |
[codex] +
[codex] +Native managers also cover the Docker-in-Docker Dev Container feature and the
[codex] +Actions, runner, and Trivy inputs in the evidence workflow.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checksum-coupled and platform-sensitive records require Dependency
[codex] +Dashboard approval. Renovate may propose a version, but reviewers must update
[codex] +the complete checksum table and run the existing verification. A partial
[codex] +proposal is expected to fail and must not be made mergeable by weakening a
[codex] +checksum check.
[codex] +
[codex] +### Digest-only Ubuntu base
[codex] +
[codex] +The Dockerfile deliberately uses `docker.io/library/ubuntu@sha256:...` without
[codex] +a tag because the Dev Containers resolver rejects tag-plus-digest base refs.
[codex] +Renovate's native Dockerfile extraction sees a digest-only `ubuntu` record but
[codex] +cannot infer that it belongs to Ubuntu 24.04; an ordinary digest lookup could
[codex] +therefore follow the registry's default tag. That native record is disabled.
[codex] +
[codex] +A repository regex manager instead couples the exact digest to the adjacent
[codex] +`Ubuntu 24.04` comment. Its replacement template preserves the digest-only
[codex] +`FROM` form, and every proposal is dashboard-approval-gated. Routine digest
[codex] +refreshes must retain 24.04. A changed comment and digest for a later Ubuntu
[codex] +release is a visible platform migration, not a routine refresh. Reviewers must
[codex] +inspect the index and prove both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` children before
[codex] +accepting either kind of proposal.
[codex] +
[codex] +The sandbox source is a read-only bind mount in a running development
[codex] +container. The adjacent datasource comments requested during onboarding are
[codex] +staged in `tmp/dependency-automation/proposed/ai-agent-sandbox.patch` for the
[codex] +workspace owner to apply from the host. The functional extraction rules do not
[codex] +depend on those comments, so local validation covers the current checkout.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Workspace image evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`.github/workflows/workspace-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by
[codex] +manual dispatch only. It does not run on pull requests. The job:
[codex] +
[codex] +1. Reads the exact digest-only base from the Dockerfile and verifies that its
[codex] +   registry index is the declared Ubuntu release family with amd64 and arm64
[codex] +   children.
[codex] +2. Performs a no-cache `linux/amd64` build from the same context used by Compose,
[codex] +   without pushing or starting the result.
[codex] +3. Downloads the Trivy database, retains an all-package inventory and a separate
[codex] +   vulnerability report, and extracts Node, Zulu, and Go package versions when
[codex] +   Trivy exposes them. The job requires Trivy's Go binary record to agree with
[codex] +   the declared archive version; declaration alone does not prove the installed
[codex] +   binary.
[codex] +4. Uploads raw build, base-index, package, vulnerability, and scanner evidence
[codex] +   for seven days even if an earlier step fails.
[codex] +
[codex] +Vulnerability findings do not fail the scheduled evidence job. Build,
[codex] +base-resolution, database-download, inventory, scan, platform, required-package,
[codex] +or artifact-upload failures do fail it. The image is never pushed, no live
[codex] +workspace or host credential mount is used, and the built image's entrypoint is
[codex] +never started.
[codex] +
[codex] +The safe local build equivalent is:
[codex] +
[codex] +```bash
[codex] +docker buildx build \
[codex] +  --no-cache \
[codex] +  --platform linux/amd64 \
[codex] +  --file ai-agent-sandbox/Dockerfile \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_UID=10001 \
[codex] +  --build-arg USER_GID=10001 \
[codex] +  --tag workspace-dependency-scan:local \
[codex] +  --load \
[codex] +  ai-agent-sandbox
[codex] +```
[codex] +
[codex] +This is intentionally the `ai-agent-sandbox` context declared by
[codex] +`ai-agent-sandbox/docker-compose.yml`. Do not substitute the repository root,
[codex] +add live mounts, push the image, or run its entrypoint for dependency evidence.
[codex] +The scan-only UID/GID 10001 avoids the Ubuntu base's existing `ubuntu` account
[codex] +at 1000. Normal Dev Container builds continue to use the host values generated
[codex] +by `ai-agent-sandbox/setup-env.sh`; the Compose fallback of 1000 collides when
[codex] +that generated file is absent, which remains an existing setup limitation rather
[codex] +than an image-scan reason to change account creation.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Inventory limits
[codex] +
[codex] +Unversioned `apt-get install` declarations do not provide patch targets for
[codex] +Renovate. This includes the base utilities, Maven, ImageMagick, and the
[codex] +`zulu25-jdk` package: the Dockerfile selects Zulu major 25, while Azul apt
[codex] +selects the patch available at build time. Renovate's `java-version` datasource
[codex] +uses Adoptium metadata and must not be presented as Azul Zulu coverage.
[codex] +
[codex] +Node is similarly declared as major 24 and receives NodeSource patch updates
[codex] +only through a fresh apt transaction. A cached image build is not evidence of
[codex] +current apt packages, so the workflow uses `--no-cache`. The current container
[codex] +baseline is Node 24, but that user-owned prerequisite predates this onboarding
[codex] +and is not a Renovate-discovered upgrade.
[codex] +
[codex] +The official VIA 3.0.13 archive and its two checked-in checksums have no
[codex] +corresponding release/tag in the upstream GitHub repository, so standard
[codex] +Renovate datasources do not provide a trustworthy update path. VIA remains an
[codex] +explicit discovery gap and must retain both checksum checks during manual
[codex] +review. Global npm packages installed as `latest`, unbounded PyPI installs, and
[codex] +unpinned apt packages likewise have scan/rebuild coverage but no version-pin PR.
[codex] +
[codex] +The exact Ubuntu base index supports ARM64, and several binary downloads use
[codex] +`TARGETARCH`, but the Go URL is fixed to `linux-amd64`. Consequently, the
[codex] +workflow's amd64 build and scan is not proof that the complete image works on
[codex] +ARM64. Changing that architecture behavior is separate work.
[codex] +
[codex] +## Local baseline evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +On 2026-09-07, the rebuilt active container reported Node `v24.20.0`, npm
[codex] +`11.19.0`, Go `1.24.1 linux/amd64`, and Zulu OpenJDK `25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. The
[codex] +installed apt inventory included `nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1` and Zulu 25
[codex] +packages at `25.0.4.1-1`. These are observations, not desired-version inputs.
[codex] +The Dockerfile and README both select Node major 24.
[codex] +
[codex] +The checked-in Ubuntu digest is a multi-platform Ubuntu 24.04 index with both
[codex] +linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 children. A no-cache local `linux/amd64` build from
[codex] +the Compose context completed on 2026-09-07 without starting or pushing the
[codex] +image. Trivy 0.74.0 identified Ubuntu 24.04, 481 OS packages, Node
[codex] +`24.20.0`, Zulu `25.0.4.1`, and the Go `1.24.1` binary package. The raw local
[codex] +evidence is staged under `tmp/dependency-automation/local-image-scan/`; it is
[codex] +temporary validation output rather than a checked-in report. Vulnerability
[codex] +scanning reported 4,381 result rows, including 29 critical and 767 high rows,
[codex] +while scanner and database operations completed. Counts include repeated Go
[codex] +standard-library findings across installed binaries and are not unique-advisory
[codex] +or review-parity totals. The existing backlog remains non-gating under the
[codex] +shared policy.
[codex] +
[codex] +A credential-free Renovate 44.65.5 lookup under Node 24 extracted 16 records
[codex] +from 13 files: one Dev Container feature, one native digest-only Dockerfile
[codex] +record, five workflow records, and nine regex-managed Dockerfile records. The
[codex] +safe Ubuntu manager separately proposed the current 24.04 digest and a visible
[codex] +26.04 major; its replacement preserves the digest-only form. Node 24 was current,
[codex] +the Go source exposed maintained-line 1.24 and later lines, and PyPI exposed a
[codex] +mitmproxy patch. The safe Ubuntu Docker lookup succeeded. GitHub-backed identities
[codex] +were extracted but reported `github-token-required`; those lookups remain pending
[codex] +Phase 12 rather than being reported as successful.
[codex] +
